name: Composite Bow
notes: Built for Strength 5+.

name: Great Sword
notes: Can attack a mounted opponent from foot without penalty.

name: Great Axe
notes: Can attack a mounted opponent from foot without penalty.

name: Poleaxe
notes: Can attack a mounted opponent from foot without penalty.

name: Sledge
notes: Can attack a mounted opponent from foot without penalty.

name: Lance
notes: +8L on a mounted charge (base +2L); charging costs defense for the turn.

name: Short Spear
notes: Can attack a mounted opponent from foot without penalty.

name: Spear
notes: Can attack a mounted opponent from foot without penalty.

name: Dire Lance
notes: Also called a spear; a separate mounted-lance profile (+3/+12L) is listed but the text gives no rule for the distinction.

name: Lightning Torment Hatchet (Thrown)
notes: Also usable in melee (see the melee entry). Activates lightning powers when attuned.

name: Lightning Torment Hatchet (Melee)
notes: Also usable as a thrown weapon (see the thrown entry).

name: Razor Claws
notes: Useable with either Brawling or Martial Arts. Adds 2 dice to all climbing rolls. Counts as tiger claws for the purposes of practicing Tiger-Style martial arts. May be made from any of the Five Magical Materials. (Caste Book: Dawn, p.78-79)

name: Lightning Chain
notes: +5L or B — normally bashing; when charged with 2 motes it may be commanded to do lethal or bashing damage, and its length may be varied between 2 and 20 feet. Can entangle a target's weapon, leg or arm at difficulty 3. Lethal soak 7. Removes all difficulty penalties for climbing. (Caste Book: Dawn, p.79)

name: Flame Short Spear
notes: +6/8* — the additional damage is gained when the spear is charged with additional Essence to cause it to burn brighter. Grants a +2 bonus to all soak rolls against heat or fire. (Caste Book: Dawn, p.79)

name: Flame Spear
notes: +6/8* — the additional damage is gained when the spear is charged with additional Essence to cause it to burn brighter. Grants a +2 bonus to all soak rolls against heat or fire. (Caste Book: Dawn, p.79)

name: Flame Lance
notes: +6/8* normally, +15/17* on a mounted charge — the additional damage is gained when the spear is charged with additional Essence to cause it to burn brighter. Grants a +2 bonus to all soak rolls against heat or fire. (Caste Book: Dawn, p.79)

name: Spirit Sword
notes: Lets its wielder perceive and attack intangible opponents. Against a spirit, ghost or other non-corporeal being, double the raw damage. Struck with the flat against a possessed target, it does normal bashing damage to the target and twice that number of levels of lethal damage to the possessing spirit. (Caste Book: Dawn, p.80)

name: Daiklave of Conquest
notes: Dawn Caste only — no other Exalted can attune to it. While unsheathed, hostile individuals within 10 meters must make a Valor roll at +1 difficulty or flee. Friendly troops within a mile gain +1 die to all combat pools and need not make Valor rolls; opponents lose one die and take +1 difficulty to Valor. Settings for 3 Hearthstones. (Caste Book: Dawn, p.81)

name: Powerbow of Perfect Accuracy
notes: The user suffers no environmental penalties and may fire with her eyes closed and still hit on a normal attack roll. Eliminates all increases in difficulty but not reductions in dice pools. While firing, the character's dice pools for all other actions are halved. (Caste Book: Dawn, p.80-81)

name: Fighting Chain
notes: Can be used by a character on foot to attack a mounted opponent without penalty. Can wrap around a target and perform clinch and hold maneuvers at a range of up to three yards, using Martial Arts rather than Brawl. (Caste Book: Night, p.76-77)

name: Sai
notes: Reduce the difficulty of all disarming attempts by -1 when using this weapon (see Exalted, pp.238-239). Normally used in pairs, which reduces disarm difficulty by 1 (to difficulty 2). (Caste Book: Night, p.76-77)

name: Short Tiger Fork
notes: Reduce the difficulty of all disarming attempts by -1 when using this weapon. Can be used by a character on foot to attack a mounted opponent without penalty. (Caste Book: Night, p.76-77)

name: Tiger Fork
notes: Reduce the difficulty of all disarming attempts by -1 when using this weapon. Can be used by a character on foot to attack a mounted opponent without penalty. (Caste Book: Night, p.76-77)

name: Blowgun
notes: Damage is Strength + 0L. Narrow hollow tube used to fire small darts normally tipped with some form of poison. Uses the Thrown skill. (Caste Book: Night, p.76-78)

name: Crossbow
notes: Damage 5L, flat (Strength does not apply). The standard ranged weapon of the Haslanti infantry. Uses the Archery skill but is not compatible with Archery Charms that allow multiple arrows per turn. Fires only blunt-headed fowling bolts (bashing) or steel-tipped armor-piercing bolts. Exceptional crossbows add +1 accuracy and 50 range but cannot increase rate. (Caste Book: Night, p.76-78)

name: Mini-Crossbow
notes: Damage 3L, flat. An assassin's weapon of feather steel, no longer than a large man's hand, normally worn strapped to the forearm; folds flat to be concealed under bulky sleeves. Its bolts are normally poisoned. (Caste Book: Night, p.77-78)

name: Siege Crossbow
notes: Damage 8L, flat. Rate 1/10 — a slow weapon normally used only from fixed mountings on iceships, air boats and city walls. Over a yard long, made of steel and brass. (Caste Book: Night, p.77-78)

name: Firedust Grenade
notes: Resources •• (••• outside of the South). Explodes on contact with a hard surface; anyone within two yards of the impact point instead receives 4L. Apply this damage if the grenade is parried or misses its target in a situation where it will certainly burst. May go off if dropped, if knocked back more than 2 yards or if the carrier falls more than 10 feet; store in a padded case. (Caste Book: Night, p.77-78)

name: Poison Needle
notes: Tiny grooved spikes thrown with a flick of a finger or spat from the mouth. They do very little damage, but a single scratch delivers their venom — so any botch results in the character accidentally poisoning herself. (Caste Book: Night, p.77-78)

name: Shuriken
notes: Damage is Strength + 0L. Rate: Special — when throwing multiple shuriken, subtract one die from the Dexterity + Thrown pool per star used. All shuriken thrown this way must go at the same target; make a single attack roll and apply it to all of them. A character can throw up to his Thrown ability in shuriken in a single attack. Often poisoned. (Caste Book: Night, p.77-78)

name: Sleep Grenade
notes: Damage: Special. Resources •• (••• outside of the East). Filled with lethe-flower pollen; everyone who breathes the spores must make a Stamina + Resistance roll at difficulty 2 or fall unconscious for 30 - (Stamina + Resistance) minutes. Exalted need only one success, and their sleep is measured in turns. Ineffective in high wind. (Caste Book: Night, p.77-78)

name: Sling
notes: Damage is Strength + 2L. Uses the Thrown skill. Can use any rock of approximately the correct size as ammunition. (Caste Book: Night, p.77-78)

name: Sling of Deadly Prowess
notes: Carved or forged from a single piece of one of the Five Magical Materials; the Material bonus is the same as for powerbows. Solid and inflexible until attuned. (Caste Book: Night, p.79)

name: Gauntlets of Distant Claws (Melee Claws)
notes: A pair of bracers with fingerless gauntlets, each extending a trio of razor-sharp claws on command. Reduces the difficulty of all Athletics rolls involving climbing by 1 (to a minimum of 1). Each set of claws can also be fired as a projectile on a fine chain up to 15 yards (see the Fired Claws entry). Used only in pairs; requires 3 motes committed to EACH gauntlet. The left gauntlet has a setting for a single Hearthstone. (Caste Book: Night, p.80)

name: Gauntlets of Distant Claws (Fired Claws)
notes: The projectile mode of the Gauntlets of Distant Claws — a hook-like claw fired on a nearly unbreakable chain, useable to attack distant foes or as a grappling hook. Retracting the hooks is a reflexive action. (Caste Book: Night, p.80)

name: Ultimately Useful Tube (Staff)
notes: A short hollow tube that expands into a staff of up to two yards. Also serves as a crude flute, a snorkel or a blowgun (see the Blow Gun mode). Using this item for any purpose requires the character to spend 4 motes of Essence to attune it to herself. (Caste Book: Night, p.80-81)

name: Ultimately Useful Tube (Blow Gun)
notes: The blowgun mode of the Ultimately Useful Tube. Each dart requires 1 mote to create and fire. The attack is poisoned, and Strength does not add to damage: the blue end fires a paralytic poison (difficulty 2; 3B on a success, 6B on a failure; 4 hours/-3), the red end a lethal poison (difficulty 2; 2L on a success, 4L on a failure; 4 hours/-2). (Caste Book: Night, p.80-81)

name: Hooked Daiklave of Dual Prowess
notes: Always found and used in pairs. Wielded together, a character can take two hand-to-hand actions every turn without penalty and suffers no off-hand penalty, but cannot split dice pools. Extra action Charms affect only a single blade. 4 motes committed per blade (8 for the pair). Each blade has a setting for a single Hearthstone near the hilt. (Caste Book: Night, p.81)

name: Heavenly Thunder Leaves
notes: Artifact • each; ornate wind-fire wheels made of orichalcum that look like carefully painted dancing fans. Used as part of a dancing performance, they add a one-die bonus to any Performance rolls made by the owner's player and can attract the attention of nearby little gods. No bonus of any sort is gained if only one of the fans is possessed or used. 2 motes to attune to each of the wheels. (Caste Book: Zenith, p.80)

name: Reborn Glacial Rain
notes: A knife that appears to be made of pure glacial ice. Its bearer gains a three-die bonus to all Survival checks made in arctic terrain, as well as to any Resistance or Endurance checks related to survival in cold climes. Has a setting for a single Hearthstone. (Caste Book: Zenith, p.80-81)

name: Flying Silver Dream
notes: An ornate, straight-bladed moonsilver daiklave. On command it leaps from its bearer's hand to engage a named opponent in single combat, fighting on its own with the launching character's Attributes and Abilities and acting on his initiative. While fighting on its own it dodges with 12 dice, attackers automatically subtract 2 successes, and it has a 10L/8B soak — three levels in one attack drop it to the ground. Has a setting for a single Hearthstone. Designed so that Solars or Lunars receive the moonsilver Material bonus. (Caste Book: Zenith, p.81)

name: Forge-Hand Gauntlets
notes: (Aspect Book: Fire, p.81) Minimums: Strength ••. Exalted Power Combat: Speed +3, Accuracy +1, Damage +3A, Defense +1, Rate 2.

name: Eye of the Fire Dragon
notes: Forged in secret before the Great Uprising for use in hunting the Anathema; used by Immaculate heroes during the war and said to have struck the killing blow against the Solar Anathema Desus at Hollow. (Aspect Book: Fire, p.81) Minimums: Dexterity •••, Strength ••. Exalted Power Combat: Speed +15, Accuracy +3, Damage +12L, Defense +6, Rate 4.

name: Black Widow Razors
notes: Artifact ••• for the pair. Prized by assassins. Damage is +4L PLUS poison — the poison is not modelled here. (Aspect Book: Wood, p.83) Minimums: Dexterity ••. Exalted Power Combat: Speed +0, Accuracy +1, Damage +5L (+ poison), Defense +1, Rate 6, minimums Strength •, Dexterity ••.

name: Grand Grimcleaver
notes: Named only in the weapon table; the chapter carries no write-up and prints no Artifact rating for it. (Aspect Book: Wood, p.83) Minimums: Strength ••••. Exalted Power Combat: Speed +8, Accuracy +1, Damage +14L, Defense -3, Rate 3.

name: Death at the Root
notes: (Aspect Book: Wood, p.83) Minimums: Strength •••. Exalted Power Combat: Speed +9, Accuracy +2, Damage +14L.

name: Gauntlets of Distant Touch
notes: (Aspect Book: Water, p.80) Minimums: Strength ••, Dexterity •••. Exalted Power Combat: Speed +1, Accuracy +2, Damage +7L, Defense +5, Rate 5.

name: Lightning Corona (melee)
notes: The integral lightning weapon of the Most Terrifying Armor of the Air Dragon; not a separate artifact. Costs 2 motes per turn to use. The book labels this column 'Attack' rather than 'Accuracy'. (Aspect Book: Air, p.81)

name: Lightning Corona (ranged)
notes: Ranged mode of the Most Terrifying Armor of the Air Dragon's integral weapon; costs 3 motes. The table prints no Speed or Defense for this mode. (Aspect Book: Air, p.81)

name: Skirmish Pike
notes: Collapsible jade-and-crystal spear — full length or an 18-inch baton, telescoped as a reflexive action once per turn. Piercing damage. Mixed alloys give no Magical Material benefit; any magical being can commit 5 motes to attune; no Hearthstone socket. Officer pikes add features (stun point, shock pulse, Essence capacitor) that raise the rating to •• or •••. The standard table prints no Rate — Rate 3 is from the Exalted Power Combat table (Speed +12, Accuracy +2, Damage +5L, Defense +1). (Mountain Folk p.280)

name: Dragon Sigh Wand
notes: Standard model: Accuracy +1, Damage 12L, Rate 1, Range 30 (the figures after the slash are the smaller foot-long models: Accuracy +2, Damage 9L, Artifact •• single or ••• a matched pair). No Magical Material bonus; the ruby capacitor stores 12 motes; the lenses require maintenance after every scene in which the wand is fired. A permitted Righteous Devil style weapon (PG pp.253-258). (Mountain Folk p.281)

name: Essence Pulse Grenade
notes: Accuracy +0, Range 20, Rate 1; damage is reduced by one die for every full yard away the victim is from the blast. The jade's colour varies the effect: red 10L fire; blue 20B lightning, ignoring the soak of non-magical metallic armour; white 20B concussive force with a knockdown at difficulty 3; black 10L freezing that temporarily cuts victims' Dexterity by two dots; green poison gas comparable to arrow frog venom. Reusable; recharging costs 6 motes and a jewelled key. (Mountain Folk p.282)

name: Crossbow
notes: Accuracy +1, Damage 5 base, Rate 1, Range 125, Minimum Strength 1, Resources •• / Artifact ••. The base damage is modified by the type of ammunition: crystal-tipped armor-piercing bolts (piercing — halve the lethal soak provided by the victim's armor), fowling bolts (+2B bashing), and fléchette bolts (+4L, but the target's armor doubles its lethal soak against them). Uses Archery; not compatible with Charms that fire multiple arrows in a turn. A repeating magazine (Rate 2 until its 10 bolts run out, then a simple action to load a new magazine) adds • to the Resources cost. Exceptional crossbows add +1 Accuracy and 50 Range, but cannot increase Rate. Botching an attack roll jams the magazine, requiring a simple action to fix before it fires again. (Mountain Folk pp.277-278)

name: Mechanized Crossbow
notes: Accuracy +1, Damage 7 base, Rate 1, Range 200, Minimum Strength 2, Resources ••• / Artifact •••. A lever-loaded pulleys-and-gears model; fires the same three ammunition types as the standard crossbow (armor-piercing, fowling, fléchette) and uses Archery, not compatible with Charms that fire multiple arrows in a turn. Botching an attack roll jams the ENTIRE bow: useless until repaired by a character with Craft (Clockworks) •• or higher, taking at least two minutes. (Mountain Folk pp.277-278)

name: Assault Crossbow
notes: Accuracy +3, Damage 8 base, Rate 1, Range 250, Minimum Strength 1, Resources •• / Artifact ••. A Magical Material in the frame eliminates the risk of catastrophic mechanical failure that mechanized versions are prone to. Jade versions add +2 Speed and 30 yards of range; crossbows built from the other four Magical Materials gain the same benefits as powerbows. Costs 5 motes to attune and has a socket for one Hearthstone. Uses Archery; not compatible with Charms that fire multiple arrows in a turn. (Mountain Folk p.278)

name: Onslaught Crossbow
notes: Accuracy +3, Damage 10 base, Rate 2, Range 300, Minimum Strength 1, Resources ••• / Artifact •••. A modified socket that powers additional enchantments; must have a level-2 Hearthstone or better placed in the socket, which provides no other benefit besides powering the bow. Shoots with greater force and generates its own unlimited ammunition of whatever type the bearer desires; cocks itself after every shot using perfected clockwork gears that never jam. Uses Archery. (Mountain Folk p.278)

name: Flamecaster
notes: Accuracy +1, Damage 12L, Rate 1, Range 10 (the upper limit the jet of fire reaches — flamecasters have no range increments), Resources •••. ⚠ The table prints a Resources cost only; the Artifact rating here mirrors it (3) so the dual-nature toggle can fund the weapon with Artifact — the ST sets the real value. Single-shot: reloading requires a standard action and a roll of Dexterity + Archery at standard difficulty, and each canister of pyromantic gel costs Resources • (or ••• if alchemically synthesized outside Mountain Folk territory). Botching an attack roll jams the firing mechanism, requiring a Dexterity + Craft (Clockworks) roll at difficulty 3 before it can fire again. (Mountain Folk p.278)

name: Pyromantic Grenade
notes: Accuracy +0, Damage 10L, Rate 1, Range 15, Resources •••. ⚠ The table prints a Resources cost only; the Artifact rating here mirrors it (3) so the dual-nature toggle can fund the weapon with Artifact — the ST sets the real value. Damage is reduced by one die for every full yard away the victim is from the blast, and all flammable objects within five yards of the explosion immediately catch fire. A clockwork timer can delay detonation up to a full minute. Botching the attack roll means the charge landed somewhere other than intended, almost certainly leaving the thrower inside the blast zone. (Mountain Folk p.278)

name: Hooked Daiklaves of Dual Prowess
notes: Speed +2, Accuracy +2, Damage +5L, Defense +5, Minimums Strength ••, Dexterity •••, Martial Arts •••, Artifact ••••• (Caste Book: Night p.81 table). ⚠ The table's Artifact column prints ••••• but the heading prints •••• — the catalogue entry follows the heading, this row follows the table, human ruling owed. A matched pair of hooked swords: wielded together they grant two hand-to-hand actions per turn without penalty and eliminate the off-hand penalty, but dice pools cannot be split and extra-action Charms affect only a single blade. Each blade has a Hearthstone setting; commits 8 motes (4 each). Uses Melee.

name: Direlance
notes: Speed +6, Accuracy +2, Damage +5L, Defense +0, Minimum Strength •, Artifact •• (core p.342 Daiklave Table). Used as a lance (on a charge) it has Speed +14, Accuracy +1, Damage +3/+12L, Defense -1, Minimum Strength •• — the damage is +3 bashing normally and +12L on a charging strike. ⚠ Attunement cost is not printed on the table page and the weapon's description (core p.341) is not on disk — flagged; the catalogue entry for this artifact is blocked until that page lands. Uses Melee.
